prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Miami. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I’ll put together specific dental offices for you — but first a couple quick questions so I give you the best matches:

1. What Miami neighborhood or ZIP code are you closest to (e.g., downtown, Coral Gables, Miami Beach, Kendall, Doral)?  
2. Do you need a single implant, several, or full-arch/All‑on‑4 style restoration?  
3. Any preferences: lowest cost, same‑day/teeth‑in‑a‑day, sedation options, Spanish-speaking staff, weekend hours, use of CBCT/guided surgery, or wanting a board‑certified specialist?  
4. Do you have dental insurance that covers part of the implant or a network you must stay in?

While you answer, here’s practical guidance you can use immediately — which types of practices to call and why, plus what to ask when you call:

Which specific types of practices to call (and why)
- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons (OMS) — best for complicated extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, multiple implants and IV sedation; often do the surgical implant placement. Look for ABOMS board certification.  
- Periodontists (specialists in gums and implant placement) — excellent for implants when significant bone/gum reconstruction or esthetic zone placement is needed. Look for AAP membership/credentials.  
- Prosthodontists — specialists in restoring implants (crowns, bridges, full-arch prostheses); call if you want complex restorations, full-mouth rehab, or esthetic outcomes. Look for American College of Prosthodontists membership.  
- Dedicated implant centers (multi‑discipline clinics or franchise centers) — convenient if you want a single location for planning, placement and restoration; many offer financing and package pricing (e.g., All‑on‑4). Verify qualifications of individual clinicians.  
- University dental clinics (teaching clinics) — lower cost, supervised by faculty specialists; good option if budget is a priority and you’re comfortable being a student‑clinic patient.

Questions to ask when you call (use these to compare practices)
- Who will place the implant (name and specialty)? Are they board‑certified?  
- Do you do the final crown/bridge here or refer out? If referred, how is care coordinated?  
- Do you use CBCT (3D) scans and digital planning/guided surgery?  
- Do you offer sedation (nitrous, oral, IV)? If yes, who provides/supervises it?  
- How many implants of this type do you place per year? (Volume indicates experience.)  
- Do you do bone grafting/sinus lifts in‑house? What are the success rates/complication rates?  
- Can I see before/after photos and speak to previous implant patients?  
- What is the cost estimate (surgery, implant, abutment, crown) and do you offer payment plans or financing?  
- What warranty/guarantee or follow‑up schedule do you provide?  
- Do you accept my insurance or file claims?

How to prioritize your calls
1. Call any OMS or periodontist within ~15–20 minutes of your home or work who is board‑certified and uses CBCT/digital planning.  
2. Call a prosthodontist if your case involves multiple adjacent implants, full‑arch work, or major esthetic concerns.  
3. If cost is a major concern, call a university dental clinic or a reputable implant center that advertises bundled pricing.  
4. If you’re nervous about surgery, prioritize clinics offering IV sedation and experienced surgeons.

If you want, tell me your neighborhood/ZIP and preferences and I’ll compile a short list (3–6) of specific Miami practices — with reasons to call each one and suggested questions tailored to the practice — and include website/phone details so you can call immediately.
